sections.html:
A Kenosha seller has three options: hire an agent, handle the sale personally, or sell for cash to someone who accepts the house as is. About 99,239 people live in the city as of July 1, 2025, and the 2020 census placed it fourth among Wisconsin cities.

No matter which you pick, the paperwork lands at the Kenosha County Register of Deeds: a deed, an electronic return and a fee. The schedule and the repair bill are what change. A listing means open houses, an inspection and an appraisal for the buyer's bank. A direct cash sale normally drops the lender, so closing can follow the title work instead of waiting for loan approval.

Residents describe the city in three pieces. The lakefront belongs to Downtown and HarborPark, and Allendale lies just south. Uptown blends homes with small businesses and takes in Brass, Lincoln Park and Wilson Heights neighborhoods. West of the I is everything past Interstate 94, which locals often call "the county."

Interest varies by area. Someone selling in Wilson Heights and someone selling in HarborPark face different comparable sales and different buyers. People commuting toward Chicago prefer a house near I-94 or the Metra station, since prices here are lower.

Owners live in 58.7 percent of Kenosha homes. Treat the citywide numbers below as a sizing tool for offers. They blend every neighborhood, so a tired house with an old roof falls under them and a renovated condo on the lake rises over them.

sections.h2: What inspectors look at in a Kenosha house
sections.html: Inspectors focus on what cold weather punishes. Kenosha gets roughly 37.6 inches of precipitation and 36.2 inches of snow in a typical year, and its record low is minus 31 degrees Fahrenheit. Roofs, gutters, basements and furnaces get the most attention and show up most often in repair requests. Cash buyers simply price them in, so there is no back-and-forth.

sections.h2: Steps and costs when a Kenosha house changes hands
sections.html:
The transfer fee in this state is the seller's bill. It runs 30 cents for each $100 of value or fraction thereof (Wis. Stat. 77.22). When the deed is recorded, the county register of deeds collects the fee, holds back 20 percent and forwards the balance to the state.

Work normally runs in this order:

  • Sign the contract and start title work.
  • File the electronic Real Estate Transfer Return through the state Department of Revenue site, and keep the eRETR receipt, which the county demands for any non-exempt conveyance.
  • Take the deed to the Register of Deeds at 1010 56th Street, Kenosha, which records real estate papers weekdays between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. A satellite office at 19600 75th Street in Bristol is another option.
  • Pay off any mortgage, lien or unpaid tax at closing.

Wis. Stat. 77.25 lets transfers by will, descent or survivorship pass without the fee, as do transfers from parent to child for nominal consideration. If an heir later sells the inherited house, that new sale is not exempt, so the fee applies to it.

Most sellers must provide one. For a property with up to four dwelling units, chapter 709 puts a completed Real Estate Condition Report in the buyer's hands no later than 10 days after you accept the contract. If it never arrives, the buyer can rescind in the next two business days and get the deposit back (Wis. Stat. 709.02).

Estates get a break. A personal representative, trustee or conservator appointed by a court is excused when they never lived in the house, and so is any transfer that the transfer fee does not reach. A closing attorney or title company can say whether you qualify.

sections.h2: Getting the house ready for buyers
sections.html:
Buyers repeat the same questions, so have answers waiting. Photographs of the roof, basement walls and mechanical equipment taken before you list give you a record of their condition on the day you describe them on the form. Gather invoices for work on the roof, gutters and furnace, the items winter inspections focus on. Find your lender's contact information so a payoff figure can be ordered early, and keep your newest tax bill nearby for the parcel number and paid-to date.

Heading to a cash buyer? A brief written list of known problems lets them quote a firm price. Planning to list? A walk-through with an agent shows which small repairs pay off and which a buyer would sooner price in.

Several tasks run at once after signing. The title company orders its search, you deliver the condition report inside 10 days, and the electronic transfer return is readied for both signatures. A borrower waits for an appraisal and the lender's final sign-off. With cash, the closing date mostly depends on a clean title search.

On the closing date you sign the deed, which travels to the Register of Deeds together with the return receipt, and the payoff and your share of taxes are deducted from what you receive. Keep a copy of every page you sign for later reference. A short call to the register's office a day or two ahead, to confirm hours and what to bring, avoids a wasted trip downtown.

sections.h2: Cash sale or listing: which fits?
sections.html:
Weigh time, condition and certainty. A house in good shape and a seller with patience may do best on the open market. A pressing repair bill, a tenant, an estate or a firm move date points to cash, which gives up some price in return for speed and a fixed closing day.

Get each buyer to state in writing what they will pay, who covers closing costs, and how soon they can close. Lined up together, those answers show which route leaves you with more.

sections.h2: Selling with tenants or an inherited house
sections.html:
A leased house keeps its tenant until the lease ends, so read the end date and any notice terms before you name a closing day. Buyers who want the home vacant will have to settle a move-out date with the occupant, and that conversation belongs near the start of your timeline.

When a relative has died, first confirm who may sign for the estate. That person records the transfer to the heirs, which owes no fee, and then signs the later sale. Keep the two transactions separate in your notes, since each has its own return and its own recording step.

Each side carries part of the year's tax bill at closing, with any unpaid amount taken from your proceeds. The normal pattern is two equal payments on January 31 and July 31, but a bill below $100 must be paid in full by January 31 (Wis. Stat. 74.11). A first payment that is more than five working days late after January 31 turns the whole remaining balance delinquent, and interest and penalties are charged back to the previous February 1.

Mark January 31, 2027 as the next first-installment date. Before you sign, the Kenosha County Treasurer or the city treasurer can report how much of the bill has been paid.

faqs.q: What will selling cost me in Kenosha?
faqs.a: Only one charge is fixed by the state: the transfer fee, 30 cents for each $100 of value. Agent pay, repairs and months of carrying costs come with a listing, and most of them vanish in a cash deal. A net sheet from your title company puts both routes in numbers.

faqs.q: Where does the Kenosha transfer fee get paid?
faqs.a: At the Kenosha County Register of Deeds, when the deed is recorded. Complete the electronic return through the Department of Revenue beforehand, since the county asks for the receipt on every non-exempt conveyance.

faqs.q: Is it okay to sell a Kenosha house in poor repair?
faqs.a: Yes. Fixing it is optional, though chapter 709 sellers list known defects on the condition report. Some buyers accept the house as is and discount the work, saving you contractor visits and repair requests.

faqs.q: Do heirs owe the transfer fee on an inherited Kenosha house?
faqs.a: Not for receiving it by will or descent. Selling it afterward is a fresh conveyance and the 30 cent fee applies then. A tax professional can explain income tax on any gain.

faqs.q: What are the Kenosha property tax due dates?
faqs.a: January 31 and July 31, in two installments. A bill under $100, or a municipality with a multi-installment ordinance, changes that. A late payment can make the full remaining balance delinquent, so clear it before you list.
